title: A number you cannot type into stops looking like one you can
goal: In the Position and Size panel, a number the app works out for you, like the height of a piece of text, sits in the same rounded box as the width beside it that you can type into. So you click it, nothing happens, and nothing tells you why. A number you cannot type into loses its box and reads as plain grey text in the same place, so you can tell the two apart without touching anything. Both looks are already built and running; this makes the plain one what everybody gets.
notes:
Design review 2026-09-04. Straight from the audit that shipped the readout: queue/audits/2026-09-04-text-height-readout.json rough 1 ("H still wears the same rounded box as the fields you can type in. Only the grey tells you apart, and a box that looks like an input but refuses the keyboard is the clumsiest part of this. Losing its border would say it louder, but that is a visual call worth your eye first") and rough 2 ("Clicking a read-only field gives no feedback at all. The tip explains it, but only after a hover delay"). The same audit notes a locked layer and a stacked layer produce more read-only fields, so this is not one field. Losing the border is a look change, so open a decision card with two shots rather than guessing. docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md has no read-only field treatment at all; add it once the call is made. Related: one-rule-for-a-control-that-cannot-do-anything is the general version of this.

Decision answered on 2026-09-05: option a, plain number with no box. Both looks were already built and running before the card was raised, with the plain one behind an Experiments switch called "Numbers you cannot type stop looking like ones you can", off by default. So most of this task is making the plain look the default and taking the switch out, not building anything new. The one thing the card flagged as unhandled is the arrow case, where there is no width at all and W would become a lone letter.
acceptance: A number the app works out for you reads as plain text where its box used to be: same letter in front, same column, same height, same right edge, so nothing shifts when a layer is locked or picked
The plain look is what everybody gets, and the Experiments switch that was holding it back is retired rather than left sitting there turned on
The fields you can type into look exactly as they did
It covers every read-only number in the panel, not just the height of a piece of text: a locked layer reads as a plain statement of where it sits rather than four boxes that refuse the keyboard
Clicking a plain number still says in words why it takes nothing, which is the answer that shipped on 2026-09-04
An arrow, which has no width to show at all, does not leave W as a lone letter with empty space after it
To see it: open Photonz Next, draw a label, read its H beside its W, then click H; then lock the label and read all four numbers

The panel rules are scrubbed with it: the "What Mixed looks like" section of docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md still calls the read-only number a known exception waiting on a pending decision, and that decision is now answered
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

Adversarial review, before building. Walked it cold: the greyer number is the only signal, and it does not arrive until you have hovered a second. UX-PATTERNS.md has no read-only treatment at all, so there was no mock to build literally and nothing to argue with. Cut as decoration: a lock glyph, an auto badge, a tinted fill. The shortest version that delivers the value is one branch in the section plus one sentence swapped into the line that is already under the fields, so no new surface and no new control. Nothing here needed state the app did not have: LayerGeometryEditing already knows which fields take typing and why not. One thing the mock would have missed: a field can be read-only AND blank (an arrow has no width to show), so the treatment has to cover blanks or the panel grows a third look.

Core, tests first: LayerGeometrySelection.isReadOnly(_:) and explanation(for:) in PhotonzCore, six new tests in LayerGeometrySelectionTests. isReadOnly covers blanks, and is false for an empty selection because nothing selected is an empty panel and not a panel full of dead fields.

App: GeometryInspector now renders a read-only number as GeometryReadout instead of a disabled field, and the disabled path is gone from GeometryNumberField entirely. Clicking a readout puts LayerGeometrySelection.explanation into the caption line for six seconds; it clears on a new selection. Not flagged: it is right in either look.

Look change behind next-readout-fields, OFF by default pending the decision. On, a read-only number drops the rounded box and sits as plain grey text at the same height (21pt) and the same right inset (5pt), so the digits stay in the same column and the section does not change height when a layer is locked.

Adversarial review, on the built thing. The first build answered a click on H with the same silence it was meant to fix: a dimmed box swallows the mouse before a tap gesture on the row around it can see it. Caught by the walk, not by reading the code; the readout is now a real plain-styled Button with the number set to allowsHitTesting(false). Row height had to be matched by hand or the section lost 2pt when a layer was locked. Left rough: in the old look an arrow's blank W box carries a faint W placeholder, so the letter appears twice on one row.

Verified live in the probe with Screen Recording granted. Scripts/playtest/readout-fields-walk.json presses H on a text layer, presses a blank W on an arrow, and photographs a locked layer, in both looks. Shipped default: clicking H swaps the caption to "Height follows the text...", clicking a blank W to "Drag this shape's ends...". Scripts/test.sh green, 2980 tests.

Blocked on the look. Decision a-number-you-cannot-type-into-stops-looking-like-a-number-the-app-worked-out-for, with a brief and four real captures (a piece of text and a locked layer, in each look). The declining option is "Keep the box", which is a real no to the rest of this task since the click answer has already shipped. UX-PATTERNS.md gets its read-only entry once the call is made, per the task notes, not before.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-04-readout-fields.json, two real captures. Related: one-rule-for-a-control-that-cannot-do-anything (p3-low) is the general version and should follow whatever this decides.

Click answer shipped: clicking a number you cannot type says why straight away in the line under the fields, no hover. Both looks built and photographed; which one the panel should wear is a decision card with four real captures, so the box change is behind next-readout-fields (off) until it is answered. decision "A number the app worked out for you sits in the same rounded box as a number you can type. Should it lose the box?" resolved: Plain number, no box
Triage: rewrote the goal and acceptance to the answered decision (plain number, no box), which turned this from a build into a default flip plus retiring the switch.

Adversarial review before building, second pass. The decision was already answered (plain number, no box) and both looks were already built, so the question was not what to build but what the flip leaves broken. Two things. One: an arrow has no width, so in the plain look its W row is a lone letter with a gap after it, which reads as a row that failed to draw rather than as a row with nothing to say. That was the case the card itself flagged as unhandled. Two: nothing outside the app knows the answer, so the pattern doc still called this a pending exception and the mock library still only offers a dimmed box. Cut as unnecessary: any new control, any badge, any second look for a blank. The shortest version is one constant, one branch, and three deletions.

Core first, tests before code. LayerGeometryReading gained draftText and readoutText, and LayerGeometrySelection.blankText is an en dash. The two spellings sit beside each other so a readout and the field next to it cannot round or spell a number differently; the only difference is what nothing means, which is an empty box you can type in versus a dash you cannot. Four new tests in LayerGeometrySelectionTests, including the arrow's blank W.

The flip: GeometryReadout lost isBoxed and the whole boxed branch, so there is one look. next-readout-fields is gone from FeatureCatalog and its reader is gone from Experiments, so the switch is retired rather than left sitting there turned on; ExperimentsStore already falls back to the catalog for a flag that no longer exists, so a machine that had it set is unaffected. The sentence about the plain look moved into the next-geometry-fields description, which is the flag that owns the section.

Verified live in the probe, Screen Recording granted, Scripts/playtest/readout-fields-walk.json, status ok. A text layer: W in a box reading 473, H plain reading 38, same right edge, same row height. Clicking H puts "Height follows the text..." in the line under the fields. A locked layer: all four plain, caption says it is locked. An arrow: X and Y in boxes, W and H each a dash, and clicking the dash answers "Drag this shape's ends on the canvas to change its size." Three real captures shipped with the audit.

Adversarial review on the built thing. Nothing to fix that I could see: the numbers hold their column, the section does not change height when a layer is locked, and the click answer still lands. Left rough and written into the audit for the user: the dash is my call rather than theirs, and the arrow's whole bottom row is now two faint grey marks, which reads correctly but quietly.

Found and fixed a stale walk on the way past: Scripts/playtest/text-height-readout-walk.json had been trying to put the keyboard into H since H stopped being a field on 2026-09-04, so it had been failing for a day. Confirmed by stashing this change and re-running, so it is not a regression from this task. It presses H now, which is what a person can do, and it passes. Re-ran geometry-fields-walk and number-field-handback, both ok. Scripts/test.sh green, 3229 tests.

Docs: UX-PATTERNS.md gained "What a number you cannot type looks like" under section 4, the six-fix table row for text-height-readout is closed rather than the one exception, and the Mixed section says why a dash is not a contradiction of "never a dash" (a dash means no number at all, Mixed means they differ).

Follow-up filed: a-number-you-cannot-type-looks-the-same-in-a-moc (p3-low). The mock library still only has a dimmed input box, which is the look that was just rejected, so a sketch drawn there would reintroduce it.

The plain look is what everybody gets: a read-only number in Position and Size has no box, holds its column and row height, and shows a dash where there is no number at all (an arrow's W). next-readout-fields is retired from the catalog and from Experiments. Verified live in the probe with Screen Recording granted (readout-fields-walk ok, three real captures); Scripts/test.sh green, 3229 tests. UX-PATTERNS.md section 4 now carries the settled rule. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-05-readout-plain.json. Follow-up filed: a-number-you-cannot-type-looks-the-same-in-a-moc.
